overview: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is an island country in the eastern Caribbean, made up of the main island of Saint Vincent and a chain of smaller islands called the Grenadines. Its capital is Kingstown. It became independent from the United Kingdom in 1979.

geography.text: Saint Vincent is a mountainous, green volcanic island with black sand beaches, and its volcano, La Soufrière, erupted in 2021. The Grenadines to the south are small, low islands surrounded by coral reefs and are popular for sailing.

history.text: The Garifuna, descended from Kalinago people and escaped Africans, fought to keep Saint Vincent until the British defeated them in 1797 and deported most of them to Central America. The island became independent in 1979. Its volcano, La Soufrière, has erupted several times, including in 1902, 1979 and 2021.

events.title: Garifuna deported
events.text: Thousands of Garifuna are shipped to an island off Honduras.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines becomes independent.

events.title: Another eruption
events.text: La Soufrière erupts again, forcing thousands to leave their homes.
